verses.zh: 有一根苇子赐给我，当作量度的杖；且有话说：「起来！将　神的殿和祭坛，并在殿中礼拜的人都量一量。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a measuring rod[NOTE:2] like a staff was given to me, and I was told,[NOTE:3] “Get up and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and the ones who worship there.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Grk “a reed” (but these were used for measuring). Cf. Ezek 40:3ff.
Grk “saying.”

verses.zh: 只是殿外的院子要留下不用量，因为这是给了外邦人的；他们要践踏圣城四十二个月。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] do not measure the outer courtyard[NOTE:2] of the temple; leave it out[NOTE:3] because it has been given to the Gentiles,[NOTE:4] and they will trample on the holy city[NOTE:5] for forty-two months.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
On the term αὐλήν (aulēn) BDAG 150 s.v. αὐλή 1 states, “(outer) court of the temple…Rv 11:2.”
The precise meaning of the phrase ἔκβαλε ἔξωθεν (ekbale exōthen) is difficult to determine.
Or “to the nations” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
The holy city appears to be a reference to Jerusalem. See also Luke 21:24.

verses.zh: 我要使我那两个见证人，穿着毛衣，传道一千二百六十天。」
verses.en: And I will grant my two witnesses authority[NOTE:1] to prophesy for 1,260 days, dressed in sackcloth.”
notes: The word “authority” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. “Power” would be another alternative that could be supplied here.

verses.zh: 他们就是那两棵橄榄树，两个灯台，立在世界之主面前的。
verses.en: (These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.)[NOTE:1]
notes: This description is parenthetical in nature.

verses.zh: 若有人想要害他们，就有火从他们口中出来，烧灭仇敌。凡想要害他们的都必这样被杀。
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouths[NOTE:2] and completely consumes[NOTE:3] their enemies. If[NOTE:4] anyone wants to harm them, they must be killed this way.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
This is a collective singular in Greek.
See L&N 20.45 for the translation of κατεσθίω (katesthiō) as “to destroy utterly, to consume completely.”
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 这二人有权柄，在他们传道的日子叫天闭塞不下雨；又有权柄叫水变为血，并且能随时随意用各样的灾殃攻击世界。
verses.en: These two have the power[NOTE:1] to close up the sky so that it does not rain during the time[NOTE:2] they are prophesying. They[NOTE:3] have power[NOTE:4] to turn the waters to blood and to strike the earth with every kind of plague whenever they want.
notes: Or “authority.”
Grk “the days.”

Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “authority.”

verses.zh: 他们作完见证的时候，那从无底坑里上来的兽必与他们交战，并且得胜，把他们杀了。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they have completed their testimony, the beast that comes up from the abyss will make war on them and conquer[NOTE:2] them and kill them.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “be victorious over”; traditionally, “overcome.”

verses.zh: 他们的尸首就倒在大城里的街上；这城按着灵意叫所多玛，又叫埃及，就是他们的主钉十字架之处。
verses.en: Their[NOTE:1] corpses will lie in the street[NOTE:2] of the great city that is symbolically[NOTE:3] called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was also crucified.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The Greek word πλατεῖα (plateia) refers to a major (broad) street (L&N 1.103).
Grk “spiritually.”

verses.zh: 从各民、各族、各方、各国中，有人观看他们的尸首三天半，又不许把尸首放在坟墓里。
verses.en: For three and a half days those from every[NOTE:1] people, tribe,[NOTE:2] nation, and language will look at their corpses because they will not permit them to be placed in a tomb.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word “every” is not in the Greek text, but is implied by the following list.

The Greek term καί (kai) has not been translated before this and the following items in the list, since English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.
Or “to be buried.”

verses.zh: 住在地上的人就为他们欢喜快乐，互相馈送礼物，因这两位先知曾叫住在地上的人受痛苦。
verses.en: And those who live on the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, even sending gifts to each other because these two prophets had tormented those who live on the earth.

verses.zh: 过了这三天半，有生气从　神那里进入他们里面，他们就站起来；看见他们的人甚是害怕。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] after three and a half days a breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and tremendous fear seized[NOTE:2] those who were watching them.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
Grk “fell upon.”

verses.zh: 两位先知听见有大声音从天上来，对他们说：「上到这里来。」他们就驾着云上了天，他们的仇敌也看见了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they[NOTE:2] heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them: “Come up here!” So the two prophets[NOTE:3] went up to heaven in a cloud while[NOTE:4] their enemies stared at them.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

Though the nearest antecedent to the subject of ἤκουσαν (ēkousan) is the people (“those who were watching them”), it could also be (based on what immediately follows) that the two prophets are the ones who heard the voice.
Grk “they”; the referent (the two prophets) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The conjunction καί (kai) seems to be introducing a temporal clause contemporaneous in time with the preceding clause.

verses.zh: 正在那时候，地大震动，城就倒塌了十分之一，因地震而死的有七千人；其余的都恐惧，归荣耀给天上的　神。
verses.en: Just then[NOTE:1] a major earthquake took place and a tenth of the city collapsed; seven thousand people[NOTE:2] were killed in the earthquake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “seven thousand names of men.”

verses.zh: 第二样灾祸过去，第三样灾祸快到了。
verses.en: The second woe has come and gone;[NOTE:1] the third is coming quickly.
notes: Grk “has passed.”

verses.zh: 第七位天使吹号，天上就有大声音说：世上的国成了我主和主基督的国；他要作王，直到永永远远。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven saying:“The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ,[NOTE:2] and he will reign for ever and ever.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

verses.zh: 在　神面前，坐在自己位上的二十四位长老，就面伏于地，敬拜　神，
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the twenty-four elders who are seated on their thrones before God threw themselves down with their faces to the ground[NOTE:2] and worshiped God
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Grk “they fell down on their faces.” BDAG 815 s.v. πίπτω 1.b.α.ב. has “fall down, throw oneself to the ground as a sign of devotion or humility, before high-ranking persons or divine beings.”

verses.zh: 说：昔在、今在的主　神―全能者啊，我们感谢你！因你执掌大权作王了。
verses.en: with these words:[NOTE:1] “We give you thanks, Lord God, the All-Powerful,[NOTE:2] the one who is and who was,because you have taken your great powerand begun to reign.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “saying.”
On this word BDAG 755 s.v. παντοκράτωρ states, “the Almighty, All-Powerful, Omnipotent (One) only of God…(ὁ) κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ π.…Rv 1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3; 16:7; 21:22.”
The aorist verb ἐβασίλευσας (ebasileusas) has been translated ingressively.

verses.zh: 外邦发怒，你的忿怒也临到了；审判死人的时候也到了。你的仆人众先知和众圣徒，凡敬畏你名的人，连大带小得赏赐的时候也到了。你败坏那些败坏世界之人的时候也就到了。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] nations[NOTE:2] were enraged,but[NOTE:3] your wrath has come,and the time has come for the dead to be judged,and the time has come to give to your servants,[NOTE:4] the prophets, their reward,as well as to the saints and to those who revere[NOTE:5] your name, both small and great,and the time has come[NOTE:6] to destroy those who destroy[NOTE:7] the earth.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Or “The Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
See the note on the word “servants” in 1:1.
Grk “who fear.”

The words “the time has come” do not occur except at the beginning of the verse; the phrase has been repeated for emphasis and contrast. The Greek has one finite verb (“has come”) with a compound subject (“your wrath,” “the time”), followed by three infinitive clauses (“to be judged,” “to give,” “to destroy”). The rhetorical power of the repetition of the finite verb in English thus emulates the rhetorical power of its lone instance in Greek.

Or “who deprave.” There is a possible wordplay here on two meanings for διαφθείρω (diaphtheirō), with the first meaning “destroy” and the second meaning either “to ruin” or “to make morally corrupt.” See L&N 20.40.

verses.zh: 当时，　神天上的殿开了，在他殿中现出他的约柜。随后有闪电、声音、雷轰、地震、大雹。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was visible within his temple. And there were flashes of lightning, roaring,[NOTE:2] crashes of thunder, an earthquake, and a great hailstorm.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

Or “sounds,” “voices.” It is not entirely clear what this refers to. BDAG 1071 s.v. φωνή 1 states, “In Rv we have ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί (cp. Ex 19:16) 4:5; 8:5; 11:19; 16:18 (are certain other sounds in nature thought of here in addition to thunder, as e.g. the roar of the storm?…).”

Although BDAG 1075 s.v. χάλαζα gives the meaning “hail” here, it is not clear whether the adjective μεγάλη (megalē) refers to the intensity of the storm or the size of the individual hailstones, or both.
